correctness.rationale: PASS: The source Eq.(1) was checked directly on the main mathematical pages of the 30-page primary paper. On A=0, the virus equation yields V=kI/dV; the CTL equation yields strictly increasing I(E)=(dE E−s)(h1+E)/(cE), E>s/dE, with I′=(dE+s h1/E²)/c>0. The infected-cell equilibrium determines S=D(E)(dV+σkI)/(βk), and the susceptible balance gives strictly increasing Fβ(E)=D(E)[dS dV/(βk)+(1+dSσ/β)I(E)]=λ. This has precisely one solution iff β>βc=dS dV(dI+p s/dE)/(kλ). Symbolic differentiation independently checked all five reduced balance equations and the C formula. Transverse antibody eigenvalue ωV/h2−dA crosses zero only at IA=dA dV h2/(ωk), giving finite βA iff λ>DA IA, with exact stated βA>βc. It does not establish full local stability, global attractivity, or a transcritical exchange.
